quest.title: All Names Are Noble
quest.description: Your adventures in Natlan continue. After some time has passed...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x600, Mora x26025, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x5

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: I see, thank you so much. The Adventurers' Guild has been overwhelmed these days...

dialogues.speaker: Piltzin
dialogues.text: No worries at all. We've always valued the strength of adventurers. Given the current situation, it's vital that we all work together.

dialogues.speaker: Piltzin
dialogues.text: Since we're facing the same enemies, I'll send you the intel we've collected on the Abyss so far. Then we can take a look at how to coordinate our efforts.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Alright, thank you so much.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hi Katheryne, it's us! Got any new commissions?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Ah, you two have come just on time. I've got some good news — the Pyro Archon has finished assembling her forces and stationed them all across Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Given how the Abyss has ramped up its activities lately, we can no longer afford to act only after receiving news of an invasion.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: So, the Pyro Archon suggested that the Scions of the Canopy and the Adventurers' Guild focus on collecting and disseminating intel. That way, we can stay informed of everything that's happening across the land.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Once we receive word of enemy activity, we can notify the nearest camp and the stationed forces can take immediate action.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That'll lead to a faster response time.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Yes, precisely. This should also allow us to focus on gathering information, rather than running around and trying to tackle everything at once.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: So please also take a chance to relax, you two. You've been working hard these days and this will be a good opportunity for some well-deserved rest.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's the plan! Phew, we can finally stop and take a break.

choices.text: But the threat of the Abyss is still far from over.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon knows that! It's not like Paimon just wanted to lay here and do nothing.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Hehe, the movements of the Abyss are always unpredictable. There have also been times when it suddenly became more active in the past. The people here generally see it as something like an acute natural disaster.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Once the disaster is over, everyone will return to their normal lives. We just all hope that day will be sooner rather than later.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right, most people have no idea just how bad the situation has gotten in the Night Kingdom...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I also hope the day of peace will come soon.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: #Eh? Is that {NICKNAME} and Paimon? Hello hello!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh hey, Kachina! Are you feeling better now?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Hehe, yep! Now really isn't the time to stay at home and recover, anyway. I wanted to do something to help.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: I heard that the Pyro Archon is gathering warriors to be stationed in the more remote areas, so I came here to sign up!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Hehe, don't think I haven't heard about all the things that you've been doing! With everyone working so hard, I've got to do my part too.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Oh, by the way, Xilonen told me she was ordered to forge you an Ancient Name!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: She said that she's all set and we can head over whenever we're ready.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, so we'll finally get to meet Xilonen! The legendary forger of Ancient Names... Paimon still can't believe anyone could forge those things!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Hehe, Xilonen is a true master! Not only can she forge Ancient Names, but also all sorts of new and fun things.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: She's always got a pile of commissions on her plate, so you usually have to wait a while before she finishes something. In this case, though, she's completely cleared her schedule just to work with you. She wants to give your name her full attention!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Then we should properly thank her when we meet.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Well, I've already signed up as a warrior, so all I have to do for now is wait for my assignment... If it's okay, maybe we can go to see Xilonen together?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: She wouldn't turn me away, right? I mean, I hope she wouldn't...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, have some confidence in yourself, Kachina! After all, you're already a victor of the Night Warden Wars!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Ahhhh...!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: On second thought, m—maybe I'll just find a hole in the ground to jump into and hide for a while!

choices.text: You're the future of your tribe.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Mhm! I'll do my best and also make sure to stay out of your way. The last thing I want is to add to your work!

choices.text: But the less work we take, the less we'll earn...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Keeping Natlan safe and sound is our priority now, the Mora can wait!

talks.objective: Go to the Children of Echoes

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Xilonen, I've brought the person who needs an Ancient Name!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: #{M#He's super amazing and I've already learned tons of stuff from him! I can vouch that he's really worthy of a hero's name!}{F#She's super amazing and I've already learned tons of stuff from her! I can vouch that she's really worthy of a hero's name!}

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Ah yes, so I've heard. So young and yet you've already got quite the reputation...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: ...Wait. Are you... outlanders?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep, we're travelers who just arrived in Natlan not too long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: No, I mean... I was aware that you're travelers... It's just, no one told me that you're outlanders.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Huh? You're saying the Pyro Archon didn't tell you?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: #{M#No. The only thing she said is that a new hero had pledged himself to the plan, but we'd need to forge an Ancient Name to ensure he'd be able to return safe and sound.}{F#No. The only thing she said is that a new hero had pledged herself to the plan, but we'd need to forge an Ancient Name to ensure she'd be able to return safe and sound.}

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: She did mention that it would be quite difficult to forge an Ancient Name for them, but at the time I thought she was just commenting on my skills...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: But I seem to understand where the true difficulty lies now, ahaha.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: A—Are you upset?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I wouldn't go that far. I'm used to it, really — I just need a moment to process things.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: The Pyro Archon's requests are always difficult to fulfill and we used to argue a lot. Honestly, it's probably for the better that she didn't bring this up at the time.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Anyway, I can't argue with her if she isn't here. It'd be pointless to take my anger out on someone else.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: But just because I understand her rationale doesn't make me any less upset. After all, she must have known that forging an Ancient Name for an outlander is an impossible task!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's... impossible?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: As you probably know, an Ancient Name is a symbol of a hero's spirit and glory, which grows even richer and heavier as generations of successors inherit it.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: We forge Ancient Names by engraving the heroic deeds of an individual who will become the first hero of that particular Name.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I've got plenty of deeds under my belt.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Y—Yeah, I saw countless feats recorded in their Adventure Handbook! It felt like they could do anything!

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: But they were all performed outside of Natlan, correct?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's right...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Then those deeds haven't been recorded by the Night Kingdom. To take it one step further, even if you had performed heroic deeds in Natlan, as an outlander, your actions still wouldn't have been recorded by our lands.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Only memories and experiences that have been acknowledged by the Wayob can be used as the basis for an Ancient Name.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Even the greatest of craftsmen cannot create something out of thin air, you know. That's just how it is.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seems the Wayob don't want just anyone to get a Name, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Mavuika of all people should know better than anyone, yet she still entrusted the task of forging the Ancient Name to me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon gets it... Nobody's happy being asked to do the impossible.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Why do I feel like this has happened before... I think last time, Xilonen just ended up running dozens of laps around the hills nearby...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Don't remind me. Let's just focus on how we can pull this off... how to achieve the impossible.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, you mean you're already willing to accept the task!?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Well, what else can I do? What's happened is already done, and it's not like I can outright defy the order of my Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: If she gave me this order, then she believes the Ancient Name is an indispensable part of her plan and that I'll be able to find a way to make it happen.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: In other words, the order is an affirmation of my abilities.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, not only has she accepted the task, but now she's looking for silver linings!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe that's just how much she and the Archon trust each other.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Y—Yeah, let's see if we can find some special way to pull this off! If we really can't make it work, uh, I'm sure we can still go back and talk to the Pyro Archon, right?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: #{M#The key is getting the Wayob to somehow acknowledge the Traveler's existence and record his heroic deeds.}{F#The key is getting the Wayob to somehow acknowledge the Traveler's existence and record her heroic deeds.}

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We heard the voice of a Wayob when we were in the Night Kingdom before. We even had a whole conversation with her!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If we can talk to her again, maybe we can figure something out together.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Well, every tribe has their own Wayob. How do we know if the one you met is indeed the best one for us to talk to?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Plus, considering the unprecedented nature of the situation, I have a feeling that the acknowledgment of one Wayob alone would probably not be enough.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Would we need to gain the acknowledgement of all six Wayob?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: *sigh* I don't know. That requires a level of knowledge that I do not possess.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: We need to find a consultant who's an expert on all things Night Kingdom and Wayob. The first person who comes to mind is Citlali at the Masters of the Night-Wind, the one we call "Granny Itztli."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohh, we've heard of that name before! We used her Spiritspeaker Stone to find Kachina's Ancient Name!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A person who can make something like that must be pretty impressive. Paimon's sure she'd be able to help!

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Still, she's older now, and quite eccentric. It's hard to even book a meeting with her, given that she's constantly holed up in her room and doesn't like to be disturbed.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I've heard that to get her help, you have to be extremely patient with her and know how to keep her spirit up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, hate to break it to ya, but...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: She probably won't be very happy with us.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Huh? Why's that? Didn't she already help you before? And you even managed to save Kachina.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, yeah... at the cost of her Spiritspeaker Stone being... split into two.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Great going, Mavuika. We're already off to a rocky start here.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: In that case, I guess your only option is to try to emphasize that this is an important order from the Pyro Archon. Hopefully, Citlali would still want to show respect to the Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I'll also write a letter on your behalf. If you can find someone to deliver it and mention some good things about you, then that should help too...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Oh, let's ask Kinich to deliver the letter! He understands the whole situation and is already a familiar face to her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon sure hopes Ajaw won't interrupt when he's talking though...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Alright. Kinich's a seasoned negotiator, I trust that he'll know the best things to say.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Great, then I'll go contact him right now!

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Please give me a moment to write the letter. We can meet up near the Statue of The Seven later.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds good! We'll take a stroll in the meantime.

talks.objective: Go and meet up with Kinich at the agreed location

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Kinich makes his way over after some time.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: We meet again. Kachina told me everything — I'll deliver the message to the Masters of Night-Wind and convince Citlali to give you a chance.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I'll also take this chance to explain what happened to the Spiritspeaker Stone and offer her an apology in person.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Sorry to put this on you, Kinich. It's just that you're probably the only person who knows how to deal with her.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: It's alright. We're all working for the sake of the Pyro Archon's plan, after all. Everyone here understands how dire the situation has become.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Oh, wait. So Kachina and the Traveler also know about the plan?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Mhm, because we all saw a hero of the past re-materialize right before our eyes! And then Mualani said that a ton of knowledge and memories suddenly flooded her brain.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: The Pyro Archon explained everything when we came back from the Night Kingdom, including the reason behind the appearance of the hero, as well as the current state of the Night Kingdom.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right! She mentioned there are six heroes, and that Xilonen is one of four that have already been acknowledged.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Hehe, then I suppose there's no need to keep any secrets between us. Having companions walk by your side is perhaps the best solace when facing such a bleak reality.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I have another piece of intel to share. We've pretty much identified the person who rescued The Captain in the Stadium of the Sacred Flame.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: His name is Ororon, and he also hails from the Masters of the Night-Wind. However, he's spent most of his life living out in the wilderness by himself, away from the rest of the tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: That's why his disappearance went unnoticed. By the time Citlali finally realized that he was gone, no one had heard from him for quite a while.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Citlali knows him, too?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: That's right. Ororon was an orphan raised by the chief of the Masters of the Night-Wind and many other kindhearted people in his tribe. Still, he's had something of an odd reputation his whole life.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Odd, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Given how the Masters of the Night-Wind love to babble about dreams and revelations, they're already a pretty strange bunch to most.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I've never met Ororon, but if even they consider him the odd one... he's gotta be pretty far out there.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: That's right. So, in that sense, Ororon and Citlali actually have quite a bit in common, which is why they get along pretty well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, makes sense! But Paimon wonders how Citlali could be the first one to notice Ororon's disappearance if she spends the whole day in her room.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: As of now, we still haven't been able to confirm whether Ororon joined the Fatui voluntarily, or if he was coerced.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Citlali is probably eager to prove that Ororon hasn't betrayed his people. I plan to use this as leverage when I go to talk with her.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: If I'm following, you mean we'll help her investigate Ororon and The Captain's whereabouts?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Yes. If you're all on board with the idea, then it becomes a mutually beneficial collaboration, rather than just a one-sided request.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Even though I don't think Citlali is the kind of person to turn down an order from the Pyro Archon, working together with us will help her focus and not get distracted by the whole Ororon situation.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah. Plus we kinda owe her one anyway to make up for breaking the Spiritspeaker Stone.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: This is a pretty well-thought-out plan. As expected of "Mal{RUBY#[D]Turnfire}ipo" Kinich.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Then I'll leave my letter to you. Let's hope Citlali can meet at the Stadium in two days.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Sure, I'll head out right away.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Take care out there, Kinich!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: I'll be heading back as well. There are still a few things I need to pack.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Okay, then let's part ways for now. I'll see you in a couple of days.

choices.text: This way, we can get two birds with one stone.

talks.objective: Wait until the morning of the day after tomorrow

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Xilonen! How's everything going?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: #Oh, hi {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I have bad news... Citlali did not reply to our request. Although, I suppose I'm not too surprised...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You mean she didn't even bother to give Kinich a response? Guess she really does have quite an ego, then...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: She can also be quite eccentric, though she's one of the most gifted people around. Even the Masters of the Night-Wind often struggle to work with her. My guess is that she probably has other reasons for not deigning us with a response.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: But let's go to the Stadium and see if we can meet her there. If we do get a chance to talk to her in person, we can still try to work something out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's true. Let's go!

talks.objective: Go to the agreed location and wait for Citlali

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You arrive at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. As expected, Citlali is not there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon doesn't see anybody... Seems she's just not gonna show up, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: *sigh* Well, we tried to be as considerate as we could, but she's under no obligation to help.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That might be true, but this is still a request from the Pyro Archon, right? Shouldn't a subject always answer the call of their archon?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: A subject? Well... If you ask me, I'd say we're all more like friends with the archon.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Yes, Mavuika is our leader, but that doesn't mean there's any kind of tall barrier between us and her.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: The only thing is that she often has... very high expectations of us.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I can tell.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, so even though she's super powerful, it sounds like she's actually pretty down-to-earth and easy to get along with.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Unlike that old hag, "Granny Itztli," right? Does she think she can ignore us just because she's famous!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You all talk about her like she's some kind of huge deal, but she didn't even bother to reply to our letter! Seriously, even if she didn't want to come, she could at least let us know!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If that's what aging does to you, Paimon never wants to get old...
Oh, really? So that's how you see me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? Who's there? Who's talking next to Paimon!?
Oh, don't mind me — I'm just a disgruntled old hag, right? Come on, relax. I'm sure my bark's worse than my bite.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Huh? Citlali...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, you're Citlali? You're... "Granny" Itztli!?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Yes, Granny Itztli — but emphasis on "Itztli," not granny.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You must know this trope from light novels, surely? They use it all the time: the young man who's actually the oldest person in the room... the girl next door who turns out to be a seasoned veteran... The wise sage who looks like a little kid...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Oh, wipe that look off your face. You've seriously never seen an older lady that doesn't look her age? Okay, well, don't go thinking it's a trick, either. See? I'm barely wearing any makeup...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Did I forget to mention? She's called "Granny," but uh... she's actually pretty young.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And you were complaining about the Pyro Archon leaving things out...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: It was an honest mistake! I guess we've just gotten used to it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, Paimon's sorry... So, how old are you, actually?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: How dare you! Don't you know it's rude to ask a lady her age?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, Paimon really didn't mean to offend you, it's just that... Your case seems really... unique!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, Paimon just wanted to apologize, but now she's putting more and more of her foot in her mouth... Really, Paimon just got a little mad, since we thought, well... you were going to leave us out to dry...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: It was my idea to invite you here, Citlali. So if you're upset, you can just take it out on me.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...Alright, I was only joking, I didn't mean to chastise anyone. There's really no need to take all this so seriously — if anything, I'm gonna feel awkward if we keep this going, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I received Kinich's letter and was planning to attend this meeting. Since I had already decided to come, I figured there was no need to draft a reply that simply said "understood." Besides, just showing up is the most important part, no?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: But, of course...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: It's also natural for people to get held up by one thing or another as they're trying to leave the house! Haha, it certainly was a bit awkward to see that everyone else had arrived before me...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: At first, I was thinking of quietly sneaking over, but since you were already here waiting for me, I started thinking about how I should phrase my apology... Only to hear you all talking smack about me. Oh, my days...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...Hmph. Anyway, that's the whole story. Uh, ahem... Honestly, it's not like I owed you an explanation, anyway!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Huh? What's with that expression...?)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Was she feeling embarrassed just now!?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Is she waiting for us to carry on the conversation? Everything she's saying sounds like a joke, but I'm not sure if I should laugh... Would it be rude to laugh? Or even more rude not to laugh?)

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: (When the Masters of the Night-Wind say they struggle dealing with her... I wonder if the feeling is mutual. She seems to be pretty awkward herself... Everything she does and says seems a bit forced.)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ahem... Anyway, Xilonen, I heard that you require my help in crafting an Ancient Name?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Correct. The situation isn't like anything we've handled before. Let me explain...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Xilonen explains the Pyro Archon's request as well as the difficulties she's encountered.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I see... So Mavuika has asked you to forge an Ancient Name for an outlander. Well, that would be a first.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: And you've also heard all about Ororon. I must say, he's always been a good kid. I can't see him joining the Fatui of his own volition — he must have been coerced somehow.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We'll know once we find him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! That's what we came here to ask you. We'll help bring Ororon back if you help us solve the problems of forging the Ancient Name. What do you think?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #Hmm... I suppose I'll just call you {NICKNAME} for now. {NICKNAME}, come here. Let me take a good look at you.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: "Wealth leads to unending conflicts between people, yet you alone transcend the value of gold. Baleful thunder and wrathful waves bring terror to mortal hearts, yet again and again, you've braved them to find new worlds."

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: "O weary yet free soul, even the most verdant leaf in the forest will pray for your happiness and safe passage."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Excuse me. What was all that supposed to mean?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Those are all things that I could see in you. You've experienced far more than even most mortals could dream of. You possess the heart of a sincere hero, along with the conviction to lift a torch above your head and walk headlong into the night.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Huh? Don't move. There's something here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Huh? Wh—What thing? Don't scare Paimon! Is {NICKNAME} gonna be okay?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...Shoo!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: That should do it. You've just returned from the Night Kingdom, so some fragments of souls were still stuck to your body. No need to worry, I've just cleared out the last of them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eek! Isn't that kind of like... having part of a ghost come back with you...?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: It's nothing as serious as that. If left unattended, the most it could do is stir up some chaos in your mind and generally worsen your mood.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: In that case, better to get rid of them.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: It was nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Xilonen, let's follow your proposal. Once you've brought Ororon back, I'll take you to see the Lord of the Night.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Lord of the Night? But don't we need to talk to the Wayob of the tribes...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Something this important is beyond their jurisdiction. Only the Lord of the Night can decide whether we can grant an Ancient Name to one who does not hail from our lands.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The Lord of the Night is an ancient entity that rules over the entire Night Kingdom, constantly borrowing the power of the Sacred Flame to combat corrosion from the Abyss.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so you're basically saying it's even more powerful than the Wayob of the tribes! Well, that sorta makes sense, being the lord of the entire Night Kingdom and all.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Not exactly — it's not so much that one's more powerful than the other... Ugh, but never mind, that's not important. It would take too much time to explain.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Just listen carefully to what I'm about to tell you. The Lord of the Night is currently in a deep slumber, and we can only communicate with its consciousness while in a "trance." In other words... in a dream.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: But I will need to prepare a few more things if we are to hold a ceremony to achieve the state of the trance. I'll make a list. Can any of you get everything for me?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I can go. It'll probably be a long list, so better leave it to someone who knows all the local vendors.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds good! Then we'll go with Citlali to track down Ororon.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: The Fatui are nothing to scoff at, so please be careful during your investigation. If you need any help, just come find me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep, we'll be sure to play it safe!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Alright, now it's time for us to catch that brat and bring him back. Phew...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I'm sorry I made you wait earlier. It was actually because I decided to swing by Ororon's place to look for clues.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: He has always lived alone, and I found a broken jar in his house. There was also something off about his Phlogiston Aphids — which I assume is because their keeper has been gone for quite some time.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: And interestingly enough, I saw some slash marks in the house that did not match any of our local weapons... My guess is that they were left by Snezhnayan arms.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, sounds like the Fatui broke into his house and took him hostage.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: But why would they kidnap a kid who just spends his days living in the country and raising Aphids? He's only in his twenties. What would they want with him?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ahem! That's not to say that I believe he's totally innocent, of course. Since he's the only one who was kidnapped out of everyone in Natlan, he must have done something to attract their attention.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: In any case, we'll get to the bottom of this once we manage to get him back here.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I'm truly sorry to put you two through all this trouble with me, but please help me get him back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You can count on us!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Alright, then let's start by heading to where Ororon was seen last.
